idiom_name: duck typing; respond_to? and module mixins
implementation_notes: Ruby objects are defined by the messages they respond to, so code that needs a drawable simply sends draw to whatever it is handed - no base class, no declared interface, no erasure machinery. When a check is unavoidable, respond_to?(:draw) tests capability rather than type, and a Module included (or prepended) into otherwise unrelated classes is the idiomatic way to give them shared behaviour without a common ancestor. Where the set of shapes is closed, a case/when over the value, or a small value object, is clearer than a capability check.
pitfalls: NoMethodError replaces a compile error: a missing method fails only when that path runs, which pushes the contract into tests or a respond_to? check at the boundary.
respond_to? answers a question about methods, not meaning: method_missing and respond_to_missing? can make an object claim capabilities inconsistently unless both are implemented together.
Re-opening classes or monkey-patching to add protocol methods changes behaviour process-wide and hides the contract; prefer an adapter object or a deliberately included mixin.
